Move to a later time — Posponer / aplazar.
They postponed the meeting until Friday.
Put off doing something — Dejar para después.
Don't postpone the decision any longer.
Agree or give permission — Consentir / acceder.
Her parents consented to the trip.
He took the car without my consent.
v|As a noun it is uncountable: give your consent, not a consent.
Very big and heavy — Enorme / macizo/a.
A massive rock blocked the road.
Very large in amount or effect — Masivo/a.
The company made a massive investment.
Massive is about size or weight, not only number.
Small sealed container or cabin — Cápsula.
Also time capsule: a box left for the future.
Keep safe from harm or change — Preservar / conservar.
We must preserve these old buildings.
Keep food from going bad — Conservar.
Condemn in public — Denunciar / condenar públicamente.
Report someone to the authorities — Denunciar.
A neighbour denounced him to the police.
The only one of its kind — Único/a.
She has a unique talent for music.
Strictly unique has no degrees: avoid very unique.
The rain turned the street into a torrent.
A flood of words or feelings — Torrente / aluvión.
He let out a torrent of complaints.
Often in the phrase a torrent of.
Feel angry and hurt about something — Resentirse por / guardar rencor.
v|Note: resent is not the same as to send again.
Bother or trouble someone — Molestar / importunar.
Please do not molest the animals.
v|In modern English this word usually means a sexual offence, so for everyday annoyance use bother or disturb.
Sad and without hope — Pesimista / desanimado/a.
He was gloomy about his chances.
Usually before the noun: unforeseen costs, unforeseen delays.
Make something seem bigger than it is — Exagerar.
He always exaggerates the size of his fish.
Person who does something for pleasure, not for money — Aficionado/a / amateur.
Not professional in quality — Poco profesional.
Neither good nor bad; ordinary — Mediocre / del montón.
A number of different things — Variedad.
The shop sells a variety of breads.
A variety of takes a plural verb: a variety of books are here.
Supported by facts; sound — Válido/a / fundado/a.
Stay alive after something dangerous — Sobrevivir.
Only two passengers survived the crash.
Live longer than someone — Sobrevivir a.
She survived her husband by ten years.
Strange and hard to explain — Raro/a / extraño/a.
I had a weird dream last night.
A weird light appeared in the sky.
Well known and important — Prominente / destacado/a.
Easy to see; sticking out — Prominente / saliente.
The sign is in a prominent place.
The feeling of being safe — Seguridad / tranquilidad.
A steady job gives him security.
Taking up a lot of space — Voluminoso/a / abultado/a.
The parcel was too bulky for the shelf.
About size, not weight. Comparative: bulkier.
Not wanting to do something — Reacio/a / poco dispuesto/a.
He was reluctant to answer the question.
Pattern: reluctant to do something. Adverb: reluctantly.
Easy to see or understand — Obvio/a / evidente.
Adverb: obviously, often used to agree.
The area near a place — Cercanías / inmediaciones.
There are no shops in the vicinity.
The church is over a century old.
Plural: centuries. The 21st century is written with an ordinal.
He smashed the door in a rage.
Be violent or go on fiercely — Hacer estragos / bramar.
v|Also all the rage: very fashionable.
A written or printed paper that proves something — Documento.
Keep the document in a safe place.
v|The noun is stressed on the first syllable, the verb often on the last.
Bring something to an end — Concluir / terminar.
The judge concluded that he was innocent.
Impossible to deny or question — Innegable.
Act against something — Resistir / oponerse a.
Stop yourself from doing something — Resistirse a.
I could not resist the cake.
Pay no attention to — Ignorar / hacer caso omiso de.
v|False friend: ignorar in Spanish can mean not to know, but English ignore means to disregard on purpose.
Invite someone to a fight or contest — Desafiar / retar.
He challenged me to a game of chess.
Something difficult to do — Desafío / reto.
Question whether something is right — Cuestionar.
Made on a very small scale — En miniatura.
Also a noun: a miniature of a painting.
The place something comes from — Fuente / origen.
The river has its source in the mountains.
Be better than others at something — Sobresalir / destacar.
v|Pattern: excel at or excel in something.
The dress has a feminine style.
Grammar term too: a feminine noun.
Get up on a horse, bike or platform — Montar / subirse a.
Fix something in place — Montar / instalar.
They mounted the camera on the wall.
Grow larger little by little — Aumentar / crecer.
Try to win against others — Competir.
Ten runners competed in the race.
v|Patterns: compete with or against someone, compete for a prize.
Fear something that is coming — Temer / tener pavor a.
She lives in dread of the exam.
He has a deep masculine voice.
Grammar term too: a masculine noun.
That dog is a menace to children.
Floods menace the village every spring.
A leaning towards doing something — Tendencia.
He has a tendency to arrive late.
Pattern: a tendency to do something. Plural: tendencies.
Think something is smaller or weaker than it is — Subestimar.
She has numerous reasons to stay.
The pipe is made of flexible plastic.
Willing to change plans — Flexible / adaptable.
My schedule is flexible this week.
Facts that show what is true — Pruebas / evidencia.
There is no evidence of a crime.
Uncountable: a piece of evidence, not an evidence.
A solitary tree stood in the field.
Note solitary confinement in a prison.
The power of seeing — Visión / vista.
Carrots are good for your vision.
An idea about the future — Visión.
The mayor has a vision for the city.
He is a frequent visitor here.
Done or made a short time ago — Reciente.
In recent years prices have risen.
A period of ten years — Década / decenio.
Prices have doubled in the last decade.
From the same root as decimal.
Plainly not true or sensible — Absurdo/a / ridículo/a.
There is a conflict between the two families.
Be in opposition to — Estar en conflicto / chocar.
v|The noun is stressed first, the verb last: a CONflict, but they conFLICT.
Less than half of a group — Minoría.
Stories that are made up — Ficción.
Set something on fire — Encender / prender fuego a.
A spark ignited the dry grass.
Put an end to a law or custom — Abolir / suprimir.
v|Used for laws, systems and customs, not for objects.
Of a city or town — Urbano/a.
The people living in a place — Población.
The population of the town is growing.
Takes a singular verb: the population is.
Saying openly what you really think — Franco/a / sincero/a.
To be frank, I don't like it.
Phrase: to be frank. Adverb: frankly.
Make air, water or land dirty — Contaminar.
He revealed the name of the winner.
Let something be seen — Dejar ver / mostrar.
The curtain opened and revealed the stage.
Forbid by law or rule — Prohibir.
v|Pattern: prohibit someone from doing something.
Enough for what is needed — Adecuado/a / suficiente.
The light in here is not adequate for reading.
Means enough, not excellent. Adverb: adequately.
Make or become less — Disminuir / reducir.
A fall in number or amount, noun — Disminución / descenso.
There was a decrease in traffic.
v|The verb is stressed last, the noun first: it deCREASED, but a DEcrease.
Loud enough to be heard — Audible.
Opposite: inaudible. Same root as audio.
